transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you tell me what's brought you in to see me today?

I’ve been feeling worn down almost all the time, even if I get a full night of sleep. By the time I get through work and deal with the clutter at home, I don’t have much energy left for anything else.
How long have you been feeling this worn down and low-energy—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been going on a little over two years now—since shortly after we moved into this older house.
Over these past two years, have you also noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, most days I have this low, gray feeling in the background. I can still go to the lab and talk with people, but I don’t really feel excited about things anymore—like baking or checking the telescope the way I used to.

During these past two years, have there been any stretches—say, two months or more—where your mood and energy returned to normal, or has this low, gray feeling been pretty much constant the whole time?
No, I can’t think of any stretch where I felt back to normal. It’s been this way pretty consistently since we moved into the old house, a little over two years ago.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly at night or that you seem to stop breathing or gasp for air while you sleep?
I’m not really sure. No one’s mentioned that to me, at least not that I can remember.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold when others are comfortable, or any unexplained weight gain over the past couple of years?
I haven’t really noticed either of those, no.
Have you noticed being unusually thirsty or needing to urinate more often than usual recently?
No, I haven’t noticed being especially thirsty or needing to use the bathroom more than usual.
Have you noticed becoming unusually short of breath or your heart racing when climbing stairs or doing light physical activity?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed getting short of breath or having my heart race with light activity.
Do you find yourself feeling very drowsy or accidentally falling asleep during the day, like while reading, watching TV, or driving?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself actually falling asleep during the day.

Associated low energy and functional grinding-through-the-day pattern support a chronic depressive syndrome rather than episodic major depression. The chronicity (>2 years), sub-threshold but persistent symptoms, and lack of remission periods are classic for Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia).
